title: Graph Distance Based on Cause-Effect Estimands with Latents
claim: Different graph representations of the same causal system relate through latent projection and fixing, which the distance measure must handle.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, separated by vertical dividers, dotted node marks latent
description: A row of four small graph diagrams separated by thin vertical lines and labeled (a) to (d) in bold. Panel (a) shows a DAG with nodes X1, X2, X3 in a chain (X1→X2→X3) and a solid node X4 above with arrows pointing down to X2 and X3. Panel (b) is the same graph, but X4 is drawn with a dotted outline to mark it as latent. Panel (c) drops X4 and draws a curved bidirected arc between X2 and X3, alongside the chain X1→X2→X3. This is the ADMG, the latent projection of (b). Panel (d) shows X1→X2 and X3 as a separate square node, which is the CADMG after fixing X3. The drawing is black and white, with circular nodes and no color. The eye goes first to the top node X4 in panels (a) and (b).
caption: Example graphs: (a) A DAG without latents. (b) A DAG with latent variable $X_4$. (c) An ADMG, the latent projection of (b). (d) The CADMG resulting from fixing node $X_3$ in (c).
abstract: Causal discovery aims to recover graphs that represent causal relations among given variables from observations, and new methods are constantly being proposed. Increasingly, the community raises questions about how much progress is made, because properly evaluating discovered graphs remains notoriously difficult, particularly under latent confounding. We propose a graph distance measure for acyclic directed mixed graphs (ADMGs) based on the downstream task of cause-effect estimation under unobserved confounding. Our approach uses identification via fixing and a symbolic verifier to quantify how graph differences distort cause-effect estimands for different treatment-outcome pairs. We analyze the behavior of the measure under different graph perturbations and compare it against existing distance metrics.
